dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a function data from the reals to a topological space, its limit at a from strictly below is left, its limit at a from strictly above is right, and left and right are unequal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The medium hypothesis includes both one-sided limits and unequal limiting material values. The conclusion repeats this and asserts the corresponding three properties for initialState.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every real x < 0, data(x) = leftState, and for every real x > 0, data(x) = rightState.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires initialState to be constant on each entire open half-line. Appears as both hypothesis and conclusion; imposes no condition at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The function taking leftState when x < 0, rightState when x > 0, and valueAtOrigin when x = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The existential conclusion represents initialState exactly as this three-case function, with an existentially chosen value at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction: both component propositions hold.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All grouped conclusions hold simultaneously, as do the component conditions inside the local predicates.

dependency_coverage.name: ContinuousAt
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function f is continuous at x if f tends to f(x) along the neighborhood filter of x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The conclusion denies continuity at zero separately for medium and initialState.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Equality of two objects of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses the prescribed state values on half-lines and equality of the entire initialState function with its piecewise representation.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: There is an object of the specified type satisfying the predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: There exists originState in State giving the stated function equality; this witness is chosen within the scope of all preceding parameters and hypotheses.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.Tendsto
dependency_coverage.meaning: The image of the source filter under the function is less than or equal to the target filter; equivalently, every target-filter set has preimage belonging to the source filter.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses the scalar-domain one-sided limits of each component and of the paired function.

dependency_coverage.name: Ne
dependency_coverage.meaning: Negation of equality.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires and repeats distinct left and right state values, and encodes distinct material values within the medium hypothesis and explicitly in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: Not
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical negation, defined as implication to falsehood.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses inequalities through Ne and the failure of continuity of both functions at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the interpretation of a natural-number literal from its OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets every displayed numeral 0 as real zero through the supplied real zero instance.

dependency_coverage.name: Prod
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Cartesian product type of two types.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The paired function takes values in Material × State.

dependency_coverage.name: Prod.mk
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs an ordered pair from its first and second components.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Pairs medium(x) with initialState(x), leftMaterial with leftState, and rightMaterial with rightState, preserving this order.

dependency_coverage.name: PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the uniform-space structure carried by a pseudometric-space structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the intermediate structure through which the real pseudometric supplies the topology used in limits and continuity.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Both functions have the full real line as domain; the distinguished point is real zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instPreorder
dependency_coverage.meaning: The inferred preorder instance on the real numbers, conventionally their usual order; its implementation is not expanded beyond inferInstance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the order used to form the strict lower and upper half-lines in the source filters.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real zero instance, whose zero field is Real.zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the common interface point, half-line boundary, and point of discontinuity at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.pseudoMetricSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real pseudometric-space structure with distance d(x,y) = |x-y|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes real-domain neighborhoods and limiting approaches use the usual metric topology.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.Iio
dependency_coverage.meaning: The set of points strictly less than its endpoint.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: At endpoint zero, restricts limiting approaches to x < 0 and excludes zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.Ioi
dependency_coverage.meaning: The set of points strictly greater than its endpoint.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: At endpoint zero, restricts limiting approaches to x > 0 and excludes zero.

dependency_coverage.name: T2Space
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Hausdorff separation property: distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Both codomain topologies are required to be Hausdorff, so distinct one-sided limits are incompatible with continuity at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: TopologicalSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: A topology on a type, specifying open sets satisfying the topology axioms.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Material and State have arbitrary specified topologies subject to the Hausdorff assumptions; no metric or algebraic codomain structure is required.

dependency_coverage.name: UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the topology carried by a uniform-space structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the real-domain topology from its metric-derived uniform structure.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interprets the numeral zero using the zero field of a Zero instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Connects real numeral notation to Real.instZero without introducing another constant or assumption.

dependency_coverage.name: instTopologicalSpaceProd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The product topology, constructed from the topologies induced by the two coordinate projections.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The paired limits are limits in the product topology on Material × State and therefore express simultaneous convergence of the coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: nhds
dependency_coverage.meaning: Conventionally the neighborhood filter at a point, consisting of sets containing an open neighborhood of that point. The supplied body wrapped✝.1 does not expose this construction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines the target filters for all limits and the unrestricted source filters for continuity. The mathematical translation uses its conventional neighborhood-filter interpretation.

dependency_coverage.name: nhdsWithin
dependency_coverage.meaning: The infimum of the neighborhood filter at x and the principal filter of s, representing neighborhoods restricted to s.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Produces the source filters for approaches to zero within the strictly negative and strictly positive real half-lines.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the strict comparison relation from an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the comparisons that select half-lines and branches of the piecewise state function.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.decidableLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: A decision instance for strict comparison of two real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Permits the conditional definition of the piecewise function; adds no mathematical hypothesis on the inputs.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict-order instance on reals with comparison field Real.lt.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines x < 0 and 0 < x in the state predicate and piecewise function.

dependency_coverage.name: ite
dependency_coverage.meaning: Returns the first branch when its proposition is true and the second branch when it is false.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The nested conditional selects the left value for negative inputs, the right value for positive inputs, and the origin value when neither strict inequality holds.

binders: For every type Material in universe u_1 and every type State in universe u_2, each equipped with a topology and assumed Hausdorff.
For every function medium : ℝ → Material and every function initialState : ℝ → State.
For every leftMaterial, rightMaterial ∈ Material and leftState, rightState ∈ State.
Under the three stated hypotheses, there exists originState ∈ State in the final conjunct. It may depend on the preceding data; the asserted function equality forces originState = initialState(0).
hypotheses: As x tends to 0 through x < 0, medium(x) tends to leftMaterial; as x tends to 0 through x > 0, medium(x) tends to rightMaterial; and leftMaterial ≠ rightMaterial.
For every real x < 0, initialState(x) = leftState, and for every real x > 0, initialState(x) = rightState.
conclusions: The first conjunction asserts both: medium has the prescribed unequal one-sided limits at zero; and initialState tends to leftState from below and rightState from above at zero, with leftState ≠ rightState.

The next grouped conjunction asserts that x ↦ (medium(x), initialState(x)) tends to (leftMaterial, leftState) as x → 0 from below, tends to (rightMaterial, rightState) as x → 0 from above, and satisfies both leftMaterial ≠ rightMaterial and leftState ≠ rightState.

The remaining grouped conjunction asserts that initialState equals leftState at every negative real input and rightState at every positive real input; medium is not continuous at zero; initialState is not continuous at zero; and there exists originState ∈ State such that initialState equals, as a function on all of ℝ, the function with value leftState for x < 0, originState for x = 0, and rightState for x > 0.
mathematical_definitions: The real domain carries the topology from d(x,y) = |x-y|.
A left limit at zero uses the filter of neighborhoods of zero restricted to (-∞,0); a right limit uses neighborhoods restricted to (0,∞). Neither includes evaluation at zero.
Convergence to a codomain point means eventual membership in every neighborhood of that point along the specified source filter.
Material × State carries the product topology, and ordered pairs list the material coordinate first.
Continuity at zero means convergence to the actual value of the function at zero along unrestricted neighborhoods of zero.

LocalDef001 combines the two specified one-sided limits with inequality of their values. LocalDef002 prescribes constant values on the entire two open half-lines. LocalDef003 supplies the corresponding piecewise function with a separately specified value at zero.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let Material and State be Hausdorff topological spaces, and let medium and initialState be functions on the real line taking values in these spaces respectively. Suppose medium has distinct left and right limits leftMaterial and rightMaterial at zero. Suppose initialState is identically leftState on the negative half-line and identically rightState on the positive half-line, where leftState and rightState are distinct. Then medium retains those prescribed distinct one-sided limits, and initialState has the prescribed distinct one-sided limits leftState and rightState at zero. The paired function (medium, initialState) has left limit (leftMaterial, leftState) and right limit (rightMaterial, rightState) in the product topology, with both coordinate pairs unequal. The prescribed half-line values of initialState still hold. Both medium and initialState are discontinuous at zero. Finally, there is a state originState such that initialState is exactly the function equal to leftState for negative inputs, originState at zero, and rightState for positive inputs.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Both codomains must be Hausdorff. The declaration does not cover arbitrary non-Hausdorff topological spaces.

The hypotheses require two distinct elements in each codomain. For empty or singleton codomains there are no parameter choices satisfying all hypotheses, so the universally quantified implication has no applicable instance there.
The strict real half-lines approach zero and give nontrivial source filters under the usual real topology; the one-sided limit assertions are not vacuous through an empty approach region.
The state hypothesis is global on each open half-line, whereas the medium hypothesis only constrains behavior approaching zero and imposes no half-line constancy.
Neither function's value at zero is prescribed by the hypotheses. The existential witness is necessarily initialState(0), but need not equal either limiting state.
The conclusion contains repeated hypotheses and repeated inequalities; these are simultaneous assertions, not additional independently chosen data.

Function equality in the existential conclusion holds on all real inputs, not merely near zero or almost everywhere. The declaration asserts existence, not explicitly unique existence, although the witness is forced by evaluation at zero.
No algebraic structure, quantitative jump size, differentiability, evolution law, physical interpretation, or relation between the two coordinate functions beyond the displayed limits is encoded.
The interface point is fixed at zero. No indexed family, time variable, additional interface, or continuity assertion away from zero is present.
ambiguities: Some foundational external declarations are supplied only by type or opaque references. In particular, nhds has body wrapped✝.1 with no definition of wrapped✝, so its neighborhood-filter semantics cannot be independently recovered from that body alone. The translation uses the conventional meanings of the foundational real, topology, order, and logical primitives; all three local predicates are explicitly defined and introduce no further ambiguity.
